title: Longest Happy String
summary: Build a longest possible string using at most a copies of a, b copies of b, and c copies of c.

contractDetails.constraints: 0 ≤ a,b,c ≤ 100 and a+b+c > 0. Unused copies are allowed when necessary. Return a string over a, b, and c.
contractDetails.output-checking: Require alphabet a/b/c, per-letter counts within the supplied limits, no triple run, and optimal length min(total, 3*(total-largest_count)+2). Accept every valid optimal string.

statement: Build a longest possible string using at most a copies of a, b copies of b, and c copies of c. No three consecutive characters may be equal. Any maximum-length valid string is accepted.

hints: Conceptual: A large remaining count is useful unless its next character creates a forbidden run.
Directional: Choose the most abundant currently allowed character.
Implementation: Check the previous two characters before appending. If the largest count is blocked, use the next available character. Stop only when every available character is blocked.
complexityAnalysis: O(L) time and O(1) auxiliary storage, excluding output length L.
